# ADR-0004: Remove unreachable nodes from the Membership Manager, with rqlite's reaper off

> **Status:** accepted | **Date:** 2026-11-21

**References:** [RFC-0001:C-DEPARTURE](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-departure), [RFC-0001:C-APPROVED-LIST-BLOCK](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-approved-list-block), [ADR-0001](../adr/ADR-0001.md)

## Context

[RFC-0001:C-DEPARTURE](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-departure) requires that a node unreachable for longer than the removal timeout be removed, that the timeout be identical on all voters, that this removal never apply to the Cloud Node, and that a removed node be able to rejoin the same generation as a non-voter. [RFC-0001:C-APPROVED-LIST-BLOCK](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-approved-list-block) also removes a blocked machine that is unreachable.

rqlite v10.7.4 has its own reaper, set by `-raft-reap-node-timeout` for voters and `-raft-reap-read-only-node-timeout` for non-voters. Its source (`store/store.go`, the failed-heartbeat observer) removes any node whose last contact exceeds the timeout for its kind, with no per-node exclusion, and the capability test `builtin-reaper-spares-no-node` confirmed that it removes a node playing the Cloud Node. rqlite also reports reachability per node in the Leader's `GET /nodes?ver=2&nonvoters` and removes a chosen node with `DELETE /remove`; a removed node restarted with its old data, `-join` and `-raft-non-voter` rejoins as a non-voter and catches up (capability tests `remove-unreachable` and `removed-node-rejoins`).

## Decision

rqlite's reaper stays off on every node: neither reap timeout is set.

The Membership Manager running alongside the Leader removes unreachable nodes itself. It tracks how long the Leader's `/nodes` view has reported each node unreachable and, once that exceeds the configured removal timeout, calls `DELETE /remove` for that node. It never removes the Cloud Node. The removal timeout is part of the Membership Manager configuration and is identical on all voters.

A removed machine rejoins as a non-voter when it returns, keeping its data, by joining the Leader with `-raft-non-voter`.

## Consequences

Benefits: meets C-DEPARTURE with rqlite as it is, keeps the Cloud Node in the Location Cluster through any internet outage, and uses only the HTTP API.

Costs: removal needs a Leader, so a Location without a majority removes nothing until it has one. The unreachability timer lives in the Leader's Membership Manager and restarts from zero when leadership changes, so after a leadership change a removal can take up to one more timeout. Akela must test the timer, the Cloud Node exception and the rejoin path in the Membership Manager failure tests.

## Alternatives Considered

### Membership Manager removes unreachable nodes through the rqlite API, with rqlite's reaper off (accepted)

- **Pros:** Spares the Cloud Node, Uses only the rqlite HTTP API
- **Cons:** Akela implements and tests the unreachability timer, The timer restarts when the Leader changes

### rqlite's built-in reaper for voters and non-voters (rejected)

- **Pros:** No Akela code for removal
- **Cons:** No per-node exclusion
- **Rejected because:** It has one timeout for all voters and one for all non-voters and cannot exclude a node, so a long internet outage would remove the Cloud Node (test builtin-reaper-spares-no-node).

### rqlite's built-in reaper for non-voters only (rejected)

- **Pros:** Spares the Cloud Node while it is a voter
- **Cons:** Removes the Cloud Node while it is a non-voter
- **Rejected because:** The Cloud Node is a non-voter when the Location has a single local voter, so the non-voter timeout would still remove it.
